correctness.rationale: The exact finite graph is given by 24 vertices and 36 specified edges. Each matching is generated exactly once by the least-unmatched-vertex recursion. The symmetric difference of any two distinct perfect matchings is a union of even cycles; a single six- or eight-cycle is characterized by the connected degree-two symmetric difference. The GP-based verifier exhaustively enumerates 120 matchings, twelve six-cycles, fifty-four eight-cycles, tests all 7140 matching pairs, and computes exact 192 and 414 flip-edge sets with BFS component and eccentricity certificates; the separate S4 star-generator Cayley verifier independently enumerates the graph and pairs, reproducing every stated numeric statistic. Both were actually executed successfully. The generated complete certificate and raw outputs are included.

originality.rationale: The retained theorem establishes a sharp eight-edge alternating-cycle cutoff and the exact connected reconfiguration graph (606 edges, radius four, diameter six) for GP(12,5), with explicit hexagon fragmentation. Eppstein describes the graph and its hexagon faces but not matching flips; Bonamy et al. analyze four-cycle flips; Ito et al. unrestricted alternating-cycle flips. The highly relevant Liang–Zhang 2026 theorem characterizes toroidal hexagon-resonance components by flux and ladders and supplies a trivial-matching formula, but provides no Nauru-specific octagonal reconnection, bounded-eight reachability, or radius/diameter census. No source inspected implies the central eight-cycle theorem; the general 2026 results are credited rather than appropriated.
residual_risks: Liang–Zhang 2026 general flux/ladder characterization may subsume some six-flip component membership statements after calculation; the retained eight-flip connectivity and its distances are not stated.

value.rationale: The 12-hexagon toroidal embedding of a canonical cubic symmetric graph makes face-flip resonance a natural mathematical object. The first alternating-cycle length which reconnects all its perfect matchings is an intrinsically motivated exact invariant: length six gives thirteen sectors, while length eight produces a connected graph with precisely computed radius and diameter. These results inform bounded local moves in dimer reconfiguration and go beyond trivial matching counts or an arbitrary finite subcase. No extrapolation to larger graphs is claimed.
